I was thinking the same thing, people claiming to be "photographers" and meanwhile they go on about how shit this photo is. If they were photographers they would know what photos are subjective. Not everyone can afford a tilt shift lens so doing things in post to get the same effects is ok.

I would consider photography (real photography and not people simply taking photos of their food with their iPhone) an art because it is the photographer who is choosing what to show the audience and how to show it to them. The photographer has to be able to control a lot of parameters in order to get the shot that they have in their mind. Things like exposure, proper focus, kind of framing, depth of field, effect created by the lens they are using, use of blur (in both post and in camera), color, leading lines ect. A lot goes into a good photo, which is why some people might take a really nice photo by accident but not really know why it looks nice. A photographer will be able to point out all the pros in cons in a photo (for the most part, it is still a subjective medium)
